claims: The Environmental Working Group (EWG) released the 2026 "Dirty Dozen".
According to the 2026 report, spinach has the highest pesticide residues by weight.

According to the 2026 report, the items containing the most pesticide residues are spinach, kale, collard and mustard greens, strawberries, grapes, nectarines, peaches, cherries, apples, blackberries, pears, potatoes, and blueberries.
The 2026 report lists bell peppers and hot peppers as additional high-residue items.
The 2026 report lists green beans as an additional high-residue item.
96% of Dirty Dozen samples contained pesticides.
For the first time, the 2026 report found that over 60% of samples contained PFAS "forever chemicals".
PFAS "forever chemicals" take decades to break down.
The EWG recommends buying organic versions of these items when possible.

The top "Clean Fifteen" items for 2026 include avocados, sweet corn, pineapple, onions, papaya, frozen peas, asparagus, honeydew, kiwi, cabbage, mushrooms, mangoes, sweet potatoes, watermelon, carrots.
Some experts, like those at The Garden Professors, argue that the EWG list overstates risks by ignoring the low levels of actual exposure.
